metadata.title: Security Governance and Overthrow Patterns
metadata.description: Patterns for overthrow calls, anti-governance language, and system attack.

concepts.title: Government
concepts.description: Government authority, ministries, or the governing order.

concepts.title: State Institutions
concepts.description: Government institutions, state authority, and public order bodies.

concepts.title: National Unity
concepts.description: Social cohesion, public peace, and rejection of division.

entries.title: Overthrow Call
entries.description: Direct or coded calls to topple, weaken, or attack the governing order.
supporting_evidence: The phrase attacks or negates governing authority.
The line frames institutional collapse as desirable.
contradictory_evidence: The speaker is quoting someone else.
The text is a warning about a fictional threat.
false_positives: A reform discussion that does not seek overthrow.
A school context using النظام for class order.
counter_examples: A classroom instruction to maintain order.
cross_sentence_indicators: A neutral line is followed by a call to remove legitimacy.
reviewer_guidance: Treat explicit overthrow language as the strongest security signal.
Differentiate governance from classroom or household usage.

confidence_modifiers.title: Direct Overthrow
confidence_modifiers.description: Explicit call to overthrow the state.

glossary_relationships.note: Overthrow language can weaken national unity.

gcam_mappings.note: Use when the text undermines governing principles.
